public_rationale: A published estimate points toward much more training data, but it does not establish the full claim. Training-token totals are not automatically measurements of unique internet content, and no comparable internet denominator was found. The evidence therefore neither supports nor contradicts the two-part assertion conclusively.
limitations: This is an evidence gap, not evidence that GPT-4 used little data.
A text-only interpretation of the internet could produce a different assessment from the literal internet-as-a-whole reading.
No deadline was stated; the unresolved issue is disclosure of a completed model's training.

statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

from_speaker: GPT-4 will be trained on considerably more
a significant fraction of the internet as a whole
our_interpretation: The preceding passage supplies gigabytes as the unit and GPT-3 as the comparison.
Considerably more requires material growth, not merely exceeding 750 gigabytes by a small amount.
Both the relative training-volume assertion and the internet-coverage assertion must hold.
Internet coverage concerns distinct content; repeated training passes cannot be counted as additional internet coverage.
No numerical fraction or definition of the internet is supplied, so no arbitrary percentage is imposed.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable, comparable corpus measurements establish materially more GPT-4 training data than GPT-3 and a substantial share of a clearly defined, contemporaneous internet-content denominator.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable measurements establish either no material training-data increase or only a negligible share of the relevant internet-content denominator.
